== Credits section (27 October 2026) ==

=== Build notes ===
* Added a Credits section from the credits page of the rules booklet, [https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Introductory Two-Player Game Rules Booklet] (1995), credits page ([https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192404/https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Preserved copy]). The Preserved copy was checked by sha256 against the live PDF (identical files). Names and thank-you wording follow the printed page; every person is linked, and the people without pages are red links.
* The Wookieepedia lead ref pointed at "Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game", which is not an article there. It now points at [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Two-Player_Introductory_Set Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20260308164354/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Two-Player_Introductory_Set Preserved copy]) (publisher Decipher, distributed by Parker Brothers, February 1996), checked against the live page. That article does not call the game the third product; that wording comes from the earlier text and was left as it was.
* Added Preserved copies to the two YouTube refs in Packaging (archive.org item youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o; Wayback capture of the TV ad watch page, checked for title, channel and upload date).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* The booklet prints the playtester "Shawn Smallman". The wiki has a page for [[Sean Smallman]], a later Decipher staffer (1997–2001). They may be the same person, but that is unconfirmed, so the credit links "Shawn Smallman" as printed. See [[Talk:Sean Smallman]].
* The booklet lists "Bob Madison" and "Will Madison" as two separate playtesters. The fan anagram list gives "[Bob/Will] Madison" for [[Imperial Trooper Guard Dainsom]]; see [[Talk:Bob Madison]] and [[Talk:Will Madison]].
* [[Mike Gray]], thanked with [[Carol Wisely]] "for turning a million instructions into fewer rules", may be the Parker Brothers and Hasbro designer Michael Gray, since the game was a joint Decipher and Parker Brothers product. That identification is possible but unconfirmed; see [[Talk:Mike Gray]].
* The booklet is copyright 1995; the infobox gives the release as February 1996. These are a copyright year and a release date, so both are kept.
=== Missing data ===
* No pages yet for: [[Germaine Clair]], [[Lucasfilm]], [[Howard Roffman]], [[Julia Russo]], [[André Lake Mayer]], [[Louise Riley]], [[Kathleen Scanlon]], [[Bill Smith]], [[West End Games]], [[Richard Hawran]], [[Tom Dusenberry]], [[Rich Cleveland]], [[Megan Luciano]], [[Darrell Budic]], [[Reg Schmeichel]], [[Sandy Borg]], [[Craig VanNess]], [[Paul Sudlow]], [[Scott Willhelm]], [[Gary Mockus]], [[Shawn Smallman]], [[Rick Thomas]], [[Dick Heinz]], [[Dan Van Horn]], [[Jim Berhalter]], [[Peter McCarthy]], [[Kyle Roth]], [[Troy Pope]], [[Lance Campbell]], [[Brad Toney]], [[Don Cory]], [[Suzy Wolf]], [[Carta Mundi]], [[George Lucas]], [[Joseph Campbell]], [[Technical Game Services]], [[Parker Brothers]].

== Full deck lists and stacked titles (10 November 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Card list now shows the six exclusives, then each side's full 60-card deck with copy counts (Light 33 titles, Dark 35 titles; 68 titles, 120 cards). Deck contents agree title for title and copy for copy across the rules booklet "A Quick Start" table (bottom 20 cards of each deck), the [https://nslists.com/swccgpre.htm House of Checklists Premiere list] "Starter" column ([https://web.archive.org/web/20181110183007/http://www.nslists.com:80/swccgpre.htm Preserved copy]) and Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2 p. 105. Ticket swccg-guild/work#251.
* Per the [[SWCCG Wiki:Style guide#Card versions vs products|Style guide (Card versions vs products)]], the 60 reprints that match Premiere Unlimited were moved from <code>Title (Unlimited)</code> to <code>Title (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)</code> (Set Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game, Set icon none, Also in Premiere Unlimited, GEMP <code>71_n</code> then <code>51_n</code>). The move leaves a redirect from each <code>Title (Unlimited)</code>; <code>Card:51_n</code> now points at the stacked title and <code>Card:71_n</code> was added. The short names (for example [[Imperial Barrier]]) are the black-border Premiere Limited articles, a different version, so they were not turned into redirects. [[Electrobinoculars (Two-Player)]] and [[Tatooine: Lars' Moisture Farm (Two-Player)]] keep their titles.
* Fixed the merged Lars' Moisture Farm / Level 6 Core Shaft Corridor table row and the repeated Light Side sentence on [[Death Star: Docking Control Room 327]].
=== Missing data ===
* No Premiere Two-Player face has been opened for the 58 reprints that are not misprints. Their white border, lack of an expansion icon and © 1995 date rest on House of Checklists ("these appear to be identical to the Unlimited cards"), Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2 p. 49 (which counts only the six premiums as distinct English cards for this box) and the two opened misprint faces from the same decks, which print © 1995. The deck-table images on those rows are the Premiere Unlimited faces from each article; whether each is an honest Unlimited scan is tracked in swccg-guild/work#240.
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* The rules booklet prints "Death Star: Docking Bay Control Room 327"; the card title is [[Death Star: Docking Control Room 327]].
* The Players Committee deck-list page ([https://web.archive.org/web/20210829115919/https://www.starwarsccg.org/pre-constructed-deck-lists/ Preserved copy], 29 August 2021) marks Electrobinoculars and Lars' Moisture Farm as having "the unrevised (black bordered) game text". The opened Two-Player faces differ from the Premiere Limited (black-border) text; the article follows Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2 p. 46 ("incorrect game text").
